evidence_scope: Targeted public-source review of candidate repos and official docs. Not exhaustive, not a transitive dependency audit, not an internal runtime benchmark, and not company OSS clearance.
selection_rules: Do not rank by stars or tool count.
Prefer OpenCode-native agent/skill/MCP extension points when they meet the need.
Select and load the task-relevant agentic capability before choosing deterministic tools; compare only plausible alternatives against the same acceptance criteria.
Do not copy candidates until source, prompt-injection behavior, dependency license closure, platform, network, and company approval are reviewed.
No candidate is company-approved or qualified by this registry.

task_decisions.reason: The installed OpenCode primary agent is already the runtime; add one lazy skill if relevant. Framework candidates duplicate agent runtime and create dependency/staging work. No accepted-task benchmark has been run.

Existing Golden skills are repo-native, task-scoped, and avoid an extra runtime. ECC is a serious OpenCode plugin/hooks candidate but its own docs call the integration beta, require an npm build, and do not claim full feature parity; inspect a narrow skill or hook only if it closes a demonstrated gap. Superpowers remains an evaluation candidate due workflow ceremony and install/update behavior. Anthropic skills have per-skill licenses: selected engineering skills are Apache-2.0, while some document skills use restrictive terms; Vercel skills lack a root LICENSE file in the inspected source.
task_decisions.measurement: Source-level comparison only; no runtime tool invocation or independent user-time trial.

task_decisions.current_choice: Adapt a small, reworded offline method into the existing golden-docs skill; retain Mermaid/SVG as the executable source path
task_decisions.reason: A bounded pinned-source audit found useful semantic-pattern-first, deletion-first and density methods. Golden adds editable monochrome output and offline system-font constraints without another skill load, installer, runtime dependency or external request. The full upstream skill remains unapproved because of default external font requests, optional network onboarding/export dependencies, broad permissions and mixed asset licensing.
task_decisions.measurement: Pinned archive SHA-256 93f6634f9a1be43d6c70417e0d85c687b9e34d3f044660a9a3fce613c82524b9; static archive/path and limited prompt-pattern checks only. Upstream was not installed or invoked; no matched quality/time, Windows/Linux, company-runtime or egress-attempt test run.

task_decisions.current_choice: Exercise an already-installed, company-approved browser agent/MCP first for interactive inspection; compare the candidate agentic paths on the same local journey. Keep direct Playwright automation as deterministic acceptance evidence, with a checklist fallback when no browser is staged.
task_decisions.reason: Reviewed agentic browser candidates include a version-matched skill plus native CLI/MCP, structured Playwright and Chrome DevTools MCPs, and a separate autonomous browser-agent/MCP framework. No tool is installed or approved here. Candidate risks include public download/update paths, broad browser and session permissions, provider/model requirements, transitive dependency closure, and security advisories. Agentic tools must be exercised before defaulting to a CLI when the company runtime makes an approved capability available; deterministic automation remains the acceptance oracle.
task_decisions.measurement: BLOCKED_COMPANY_RUNTIME_AND_BROWSER_ASSETS; no matched journey, task-time, accepted-result, context-cost, or Windows/Linux comparison has run.

task_decisions.current_choice: official Python SDK as the first candidate to stage
task_decisions.reason: The official SDK is MIT but requires Python 3.11+ and dynamically declares dependencies including pydantic/mcp-types. FastMCP is Apache-2.0 but documents a Cyclopts/docutils transitive-license review concern. MCP reference servers explicitly describe themselves as examples, not production servers. Nothing is staged or approved.
task_decisions.measurement: Synthetic contract fixture only; no actual OpenCode MCP call trace.

task_decisions.current_choice: Use deterministic acceptance harnesses for release gates. Compare Inspect AI and Promptfoo only for controlled internal-model/agent trials if they add needed eval functionality; neither replaces acceptance tests or proves that company OpenCode was invoked.
task_decisions.reason: Inspect AI targets multi-turn, tool-using model evaluations and supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but does not instrument the installed OpenCode runtime by itself. The pinned source declares 40 direct Python dependencies, and remote providers, datasets, tool sandboxes and artifact stores need scope and offline review. Promptfoo provides a lighter Node-based alternative but its own dependency and egress behavior still need review. No model-judge score is release proof; no company model trial or matched task comparison has run.
task_decisions.measurement: BLOCKED_COMPANY_RUNTIME; sources reviewed, neither evaluation framework staged or invoked

task_decisions.task: React product UI and design system
task_decisions.current_choice: golden-react plus approved company design tokens; adapt primitive→semantic→component token layering; keep UI UX Pro Max unapproved and unvendored
task_decisions.reason: Golden-react already encodes the company stack, offline-only package policy, strict monochrome, interaction states, keyboard access and acceptance checks. A bounded audit found useful token layering but a much broader upstream collection with online update/install paths, optional external image providers/CDNs, and unaudited data/dependencies. Keep only the small relevant method in the existing skill; no extra skill load or runtime dependency.
task_decisions.measurement: Pinned source review only; no upstream install/invocation, matched React quality/time/context comparison, Windows/Linux test, or company OpenCode trace. Comparison remains BLOCKED_COMPANY_RUNTIME.

task_decisions.task: OpenCode skill discovery and task activation
task_decisions.current_choice: OpenCode native skills plus Golden task routing
task_decisions.reason: The pinned plugin README says current OpenCode has first-party skill discovery and a built-in skill tool, and describes the plugin as maintenance mode. The plugin adds auto matching/context injection and dependencies including Transformers/ONNX Runtime; startup, prompt cost, dependency closure, and offline Windows/Linux behavior have not been tested. Superpowers remains a separate workflow-method candidate, not an automatic requirement.
task_decisions.measurement: No installed OpenCode runtime; no matched time/context comparison

task_decisions.current_choice: No production adapter selected; evaluate a narrowly read-only MCP first for agent-led exploration and retain existing CLI/API for repeatable deterministic jobs
task_decisions.reason: The official MCP server exposes structured Grafana tools but requires service credentials and can return large context payloads. At the pinned docs revision, --disable-write removes write operations but leaves query tools only when datasource permissions allow them; query_sql and query_influxdb can write through datasource credentials. Use --disable-query for strongest query denial, or permit queries only with verified read-only datasource credentials and an exact tool allowlist. The candidate README also presents gcx for terminal, scripts, and CI. No equivalent task was run, so this is a test order rather than a performance winner.
task_decisions.measurement: BLOCKED_COMPANY_ENDPOINT_AND_RUNTIME; pinned upstream permission docs reviewed

task_decisions.current_choice: Dependency-free synthetic contract fixture for offline unit tests; stage the official SDK and Inspector only for later protocol qualification
task_decisions.reason: The repository fixture proves a narrow local JSON-RPC contract only. The official SDK and Inspector are plausible conformance tools, but the SDK dependency/license closure is not staged and Inspector has a large Node dependency tree, recent Node version constraints, secret-storage behavior, and a license transition. No authentic OpenCode call is recorded.
task_decisions.measurement: Local synthetic cases tested; SDK/Inspector/OpenCode trace NOT_RUN

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus golden-nicegui skill; use NiceGUI only for a small Python-oriented workflow and keep business logic/test seams pure Python
task_decisions.reason: This matches the stated lightweight app platform and the local synthetic acceptance logic runs without installing NiceGUI. Do not use an additional agent or MCP unless the workflow has a distinct data/service need. Full NiceGUI UI and browser behavior remain untested here.
task_decisions.measurement: 3 standard-library fixture tests pass; NiceGUI runtime/browser NOT_RUN

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus golden-api-db skill; use the approved company MCP for structured live service interaction when it saves context or handoffs; deterministic local contract tests for proof
task_decisions.reason: Writing an API integration and querying a live company service are different operations. Local SQLite/mock tests avoid real writes. A connected MCP is appropriate for approved structured access, not a redundant wrapper around simple local commands. No company endpoint, credentials, or MCP is attached.
task_decisions.measurement: Synthetic API/SQLite tests pass; company service access NOT_RUN

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus golden-manufacturing-data skill; ask the investigator only for independent provenance/statistics review; use approved read-only MCP for internal data only when it materially reduces manual extraction
task_decisions.reason: Units, lineage, grouping, and expected-value tests dominate tool count. For small data use Python/SQLite; evaluate DuckDB or Polars only on representative larger local data, and keep AI-derived results checked by deterministic expected values. No company data or measured throughput is available.
task_decisions.measurement: Synthetic logic tests only; internal data and comparative performance BLOCKED_COMPANY_RUNTIME

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus golden-code-audit; add architect and verifier only for separable independent reviews; use deterministic static checks for executable claims
task_decisions.reason: The relevant reasoning skill and reviewer agents are already in the repository. The current secret scanner is high-confidence pattern detection, not a complete security scanner. Additional static-analysis candidates require pinned dependency/license and offline review; separate review is not proof unless tied to concrete evidence.
task_decisions.measurement: Repository secret-pattern scan pass; broader SAST, dependency and Windows/Linux checks NOT_RUN

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus relevant local skill; investigator for profiling and verifier for correctness when value exceeds handoff cost; measure a deterministic baseline before any optimization
task_decisions.reason: Profilers and benchmark CLIs produce repeatable measurements, while the agent can form hypotheses and implement bounded changes. Use both when comparable; do not compare them as interchangeable. Production load requires operations authorization. No company workload or runtime is available.

task_decisions.task: Golden release and independent project qualification
task_decisions.current_choice: Golden deterministic checks plus independent verifier; final company release remains with the human lead
task_decisions.reason: The local checker can truthfully block missing mandatory evidence; the verifier can review failures but cannot promote missing checks to PASS. Hosted CI and machine signatures would be separate evidence. No company waiver/signature mechanism is implemented.
task_decisions.measurement: Full fixture run intentionally blocks; lead approval NOT_GRANTED

task_decisions.current_choice: Primary agent plus golden-offline-toolchain skill; use one verifier for independent review and keep third-party adoption evidence-gated
task_decisions.reason: This avoids creating a competing runtime or product platform. Any imported skill, agent, MCP, or CLI needs source/security/license/offline review and a measured task benefit; the offline stdlib path remains essential.
task_decisions.measurement: Current local suite tested; cross-platform and company-runtime integration NOT_RUN
